rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed armies, idols, devils, weapons, and allies on which disbelievers rely cannot rescue them from the Merciful's punishment.
rows.anchor: Yoksa kimmiş, kim oluyormuş o sizin cündünüz, askerleriniz, ordunuz, kuvvet almak istediğiniz vâsıtalarınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God's protection, mercy, forgiveness, and ordering of life, human efforts turn against people; if He withdraws hearing or reason, all activity stops and worldly hopes end in punishment.
rows.anchor: O’nu saymayınca, O’na dayanmayınca, O’nun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers who reject God, His commands and warnings, and the afterlife while struggling only to survive worldly life are deluded.
rows.anchor: Kâfirler ancak bir gurur içindedirler. O Rahmân’ı ve O’nun emirlerini ve inzarlarını tanımayıp da yalnız dünyâ hayatta kalmak için boğuşan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds the pointed remark that, however high such people may fly, they are no birds.
rows.anchor: Uçsalar da kuş değildirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq means the material, spiritual, bodily, and spiritual sustenance that makes life possible; only God can grant it or withhold it.
rows.anchor: Maddî veya mânevî veya cismânî veya rûhânî hayâtınıza medâr olan gıdayı, nasîbi size bahşedecek?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God withholds air, water, light, perception, digestion, or circulation, neither a stored meal nor food placed in one's mouth can sustain life.
rows.anchor: O size hazım kuvveti vermez veya kalbinizi, cereyânınızı durduruverirse bir yudum içebilir veya bir lokma yiyebilir misiniz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since life cannot exist without sustenance, people should ask why they seek provision from others instead of working faithfully in God's domain and harming themselves and God's servants through idleness or injustice.
rows.anchor: niçin o rızkı başkasından bekler, Rahmân’ın milkinde doğru dürüst iman ile çalışmazsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite admonition and warning, disbelievers whom God has not granted faith and knowledge persist rebelliously, flee from truth, and refuse the straight path.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın kendilerini iman ve irfan ile merzuk kılmadığı o kâfirler, tuğyan ve serkeşlik ile vahşet ve firarda, haktan kaçınmakta inad etmektedirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever crawls face-down like an animal, with eyes fixed on low things and no regard for others, and will crawl similarly in Hell.
rows.anchor: yüzün koyu sürüne sürüne hayvan gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upright monotheist believer, walking straight on the clear road with faith and knowledge, is more rightly guided; people should consider which way to follow.
rows.anchor: iman ve irfan ile doğru bir cadde üzerinde eğrilmeden dümdüz Hakk’a giden muvahhid, müstakīm mü’minler mi daha iyi, daha hidâyetkâr olur?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human life is meant to proceed uprightly toward God, not to crawl like a low animal while seeking food only on earth.
rows.anchor: İnsan olan bir düşünmelidir. Şüphesiz ki insanlık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should first believe in the Creator's oneness and laws, follow His proofs, open broad material and spiritual paths, and walk directly toward Him.
rows.anchor: Hâlık’ın birliğine ve ahkâmına iman ederek ve O’nun gösterdiği delâili tâkip eyleyerek maddeten ve mânen doğru ve geniş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the religion of tawhid, and walking it straight means living with moral rectitude within the bounds of ethics and sacred law.
rows.anchor: İşte bu sırât-ı müstakīm Hak dini olan tevhid yoludur. Ve onda düz gitmek de istikāmetle ahlâk ve şeriat dairesinde yürümektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first practical consequence is removing harmful obstacles and filth from roads, making them broad and clean, and walking them justly without encroaching on others.
rows.anchor: bunun muktezâsından birincisi إِمَاطَةُ الأَْذَى عَنِ الط َّرِيقِ yani yoldan ezâ verecek, mâni‘aları pislikleri kaldırarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links this ethic of creating broad, usable paths to God's making the earth a carpet for people to follow its spacious routes.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ Sûre-i Nûh’ta geleceği üzere Nûh 71/19-20][^13]] وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًۭا لِّتَسْلُكُوا۟ مِنْهَا سُبُلًۭا فِجَاجًۭا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'ala can mean requested, begged, prayed, or asked; its first sense can encompass all these meanings.
rows.anchor: {سَأَلَ} İstedi, dilendi, dua etti, sordu mânalarına gelir. Evvelkisi hepsini ifade edebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the readings of Nafi, Ibn Amir, and Abu Ja'far, sa'ala is read without hamza like qāla; the reading can also mean that something flowed.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer kıraatlerinde hemzesiz قَالَ gibi سَأَلَ okunur ki aynı mânaya gelebilmekle beraber “aktı” demek de olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sā'il may mean a petitioner, a questioner, or a flowing torrent.
rows.anchor: {سَآئِلٌۢ} Bir sâil bir isteyen veya soran yahut akan bir sel.

rows.speaker: Cumhûr
rows.claim: The majority say the verse was revealed after Nadr ibn al-Harith challenged God to send stones or painful punishment if the message were true.
rows.anchor: Nadr b. Hâris ٱللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَٰذَا هُوَ ٱلْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some say the verse was revealed after Abu Jahl asked that a fragment of heaven fall on them.
rows.anchor: Bazıları Ebû Cehl’in فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًۭا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ

rows.speaker: Hasan and Qatada
rows.claim: They say that after Muhammad warned the polytheists of punishment, some asked one another to ask him whom the punishment would strike and when; the verse reports their question.
rows.anchor: Hasan ve Katâde demişlerdir ki: “Allah teâlâ Hazret-i Muhammed’i ba‘s buyurup da müşrikleri azab ile korkutunca müşriklerin bazısı bazısına

rows.speaker: İbn Enbârî
rows.claim: He reads sa'ala as “asked” and interprets bi-ʿadhābin as ʿan ʿadhābin, comparable to the wording in al-Furqan 25:59.
rows.anchor: İbn Enbârî buna göre سَأَلَ sordu, “عَنْ عَذَابٍ,”بِعَذَابٍۢ tevilinde olduğunu söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some say the Messenger asked that punishment for the disbelievers come quickly; the response promises it and commands him to wait patiently.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da demişlerdir ki Resûlullah kâfirler için acele bir azab istemişti

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: They infer that Muhammad was the petitioner because the command to be patient is addressed to him.
rows.anchor: Çünkü فَٱصْبِرْ صَبْرًۭا جَمِيلًا emri Peygamber’e emir olduğundan isteyenin de o olmasına delâlet eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the first explanation, that a disbeliever was the petitioner; on that reading, Muhammad is told to be patient because the petitioner sought to hurt him through disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh birinci mâna daha sağlamdır. Ve o surette Peygamber’e sabır emri sâilin küfr ü inkâr ile ezâ etmek istemesi dolayısıyladır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāqiʿ can mean something that has occurred or will occur; the future sense is intended here.
rows.anchor: Burada murad ikincisi olduğu anlaşılıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the punishment wāqiʿ may mean that earlier disbelievers experienced its like and it will happen again, but the context better suits a divinely decreed event certain to occur at its appointed time.
rows.anchor: vukū‘una emr-i ilâhî ta‘alluk etmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lil-kāfirīn may attach to wāqiʿ, describe the punishment, attach to sa'ala, function causally, or begin a new clause with an implied huwa.
rows.anchor: {لِّلْكَٰفِرِينَ} “Vâki‘”in sılası, yahut “azâb”ın sıfatı, yahut سَأَلَ’ye müte‘alliktir. Lâm ecliyye olarak ta‘lîl için de olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laysa lahu dāfiʿ may describe the punishment, function circumstantially or as a new sentence, or mean that no repeller exists for the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: {لَيْسَ لَهُۥ دَافِعٌۭ} “Azâb”ın sıfatı yahut hâl, yahut cümle-i müste’nefe yahut لَيْسَ لِلْـكَافِرِينَ دَافِع لَهُ meâlindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min Allāh may attach either to dāfiʿ or to wāqiʿ, and dhī al-maʿārij is an attribute of God.
rows.anchor: {مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ} “Dâfi‘”e veya “vâki‘”e müte‘alliktir. {ذِى ٱلْمَعَارِجِ} Allah’ın sıfatıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿārij is the plural of miʿrāj and the forms miʿrec or maʿrec; it denotes instruments of ascent such as ladders or elevators, or degrees and heights.
rows.anchor: Urûc ve su‘ûd yani aşağıdan yukarıya çıkma aletleri, merdivenler

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: One interpretation is the heavens and their high levels, through which angels ascend from heaven to heaven.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervî olduğu üzere semâlar, yüksek dereceler demektir ki melâike onlarda semâdan semâya urûc ederler.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Others leave the heavens unspecified and understand the term as the stairways and levels by which angels ascend with commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: Bazıları semâ tâyin etmeyerek melâikenin evâmir ve nevâhî ile çıktıkları mesâ‘id ve derecât demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: He interprets the term as exalted favors and blessings, which reach people at many different ranks.
rows.anchor: Katâde’nin rivayetine göre fevâzıl ve ni‘am ve ulüvv ü ni‘am, yani yükseklikler ve yüksek yüksek lütuflar

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the ranks God grants His friends in Paradise.
rows.anchor: Cennette evliyâsına ihsan buyurduğu dereceler denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: He describes spiritual ranks among angelic spirits, which differ in strength, perfection, knowledge, and power to govern the world; divine mercy reaches this world through them by ordinary or extraordinary means.
rows.anchor: Fahr-ı Râzî tefsirinde bu vechi beyan ile der ki: “Semâvât irtifâ‘ve inhifâdda, büyüklük ve küçüklükte mütefâvit olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: He links the phrase to the varied angelic spirits that carry human needs upward and bring the effects of mercy down, citing the angels who manage and distribute affairs.
rows.anchor: فَٱلْمُدَبِّرَٰتِ أَمْرًۭا [en-Naziât 79/5][^9], فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَٰتِ أَمْرًا [ez-Zâriyât 51/4]

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: He lists spiritual stations of deeds and invocations, stages traversed by spiritual wayfarers, or the ranks of angels.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî de bunu şöyle ifade etmiştir: “Bir de ‘me‘âric’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction to spiritual ranks is attributed to the verse mentioning only angels and the Spirit and to a desire to avoid imagining God as corporeal.
rows.anchor: sade melâike ve Rûh’un urûcu zikredilmiş olması, Birisi de tecsim tevehhümüne düşülmemek için tenzîhe riayet edilmesi mülâhazasından neş’et etmiş olmak gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Including bodily and spiritual realities does not make God corporeal; ownership does not imply that the owner inhabits what is owned, just as a wealth-owner does not indwell his wealth.
rows.anchor: “zü’l-mâl” mal sâhibinin malına hulûlü mânasını ifade etmez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' and Spirit's ascent does not require purely spiritual ladders; ascent to God transcends all bodily and spiritual ranks and signals their eventual passing away.
rows.anchor: Kezâlik urûc edenlerin melâike ve Rûh olması me‘âricin de sırf mânevî ve rûhânî olmasını îcab eylemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes maʿārij to include every material and spiritual level of existence and of the worlds through which angels and the Spirit ascend and descend.
rows.anchor: “me‘âric”den murad İbn Abbas’tan rivayet olunduğu üzere maddî ve mânevî bütün merâtib-i vücûda şâmil olan derecât demek olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns all these levels, is their ultimate destination, and transcends them all in majesty, as in the description “Lord of the Throne.”
rows.anchor: hepsinin sâhib ve mâliki ve hepsinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels and the Spirit ascend to God by His command and return to Him; they stand in ranks before Him, intermediaries disappear, and God's sovereignty is manifest with no one able to repel Him.
rows.anchor: hepsi O’nun [5354] huzûrunda يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Spirit is singular alongside plural angels, the first association is the spirit from God's command, as stated in al-Isra 17:85.
rows.anchor: Bundan ilk evvel قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى [el-İsrâ 17/85] buyurulduğu üzere emr-i Rab’dan olan rûh tebâdür eder.

rows.speaker: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn
rows.claim: The majority identify the Spirit as Gabriel, specifying him after the general mention of angels, as in the phrasing of al-Baqara 2:98.
rows.anchor: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn burada “Rûh” وَجِبْر۪يلَ

rows.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
rows.claim: He says the majority understand the Spirit as Gabriel, singled out for honor; the Spirit is mentioned after angels here but before them in al-Naba 78:38.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hayyân der ki: “‘er-Rûh’, cumhur Cibrîl, dedi, teşrif için bilhassa zikredildi. Burada melâikeden sonra ve يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ’de [en-Nebe’ 78/38]

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: He interprets the Spirit as an angel who guards the angels that guard human beings.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ise ‘er-Rûh, benî âdemin hafazası olan melâikenin hafazası olan melâikedir’ dedi.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Another view identifies the Spirit as a great angel other than Gabriel.
rows.anchor: Bir de ‘er-Rûh, Cibrîl’in gayrı azim hilkatli bir melektir’ denildi.

rows.speaker: Ebû Sâlih
rows.claim: He says the Spirit appears in human form but is not human.
rows.anchor: Ebû Sâlih ‘insanlar hey’etinde ma‘amâfîh insan değil’ dedi.

rows.speaker: Kabîsa b. Züeyb
rows.claim: He says the Spirit is the deceased person's soul at the time it is taken.
rows.anchor: Kabîsa b. Züeyb ‘kabzolunduğu vakit meyyitin rûhu’ dedi.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some note that the intended soul must be that of a believer, since a disbeliever's soul does not ascend according to al-A'raf 7:40.
rows.anchor: kâfirin rûhu urûc etmeyeceği beyan edilmiş bulunduğundan, murâdı mü’min rûhu olduğu da kaydolundu.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: He quotes some mystics who call the Spirit a vast light nearest to divine majesty, from which angelic and human spirits branch; innumerable ranks of spirits and sacred lights lie between.
rows.anchor: Bazı mükâşifîn şöyle demiştir: Rûh, azîm bir nurdur. Envârın celâlullâha en yakınıdır. Sâir melâikenin ve beşerin rûhları menâzil-i ervâhın en son derecesinde ondan teşa‘‘ub eder.

rows.speaker: Mütekellimîn
rows.claim: The outward position of the theologians is that the Spirit is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: Lâkin mütekellimîn kavlinin zâhiri الرُّوح Cibrîl aleyhisselâm’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi yawmin may attach to the ascent, making the angels' ascent occur on that day.
rows.anchor: {فِى يَوْمٍۢ} Bir günde bir zamanda, bunun ta‘allukunda iki kavil vardır. Birisi تَعْرُجُ’ya müte‘allik olmasıdır

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: He attaches “the day” to the punishment's occurrence rather than to the ascent, describing the magnitude of the punishment's day without temporally restricting the angels' ascent.
rows.anchor: Mukātil’den rivayet edildiği üzere bu “gün”ün urûca değil, بِعَذَابٍۢ وَاقِعٍۢ kavline müte‘allik olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be governed by both the punishment's occurrence and the ascent; one attachment is omitted because both take place on the same day.
rows.anchor: hem vukū‘a hem urûca müte‘allik olup ikisi de aynı gün olduğundan dolayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike al-Hajj 22:47 and al-Sajda 32:5, this verse does not say “of what you count”; some nevertheless understand that qualifier from the parallel wording in 32:5.
rows.anchor: Burada مِمَّا تَعُدُّونَ “sizin saydıklarınızdan” [el-Hac 22/47; es-Secde 32/5] kaydı yoktur.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some think the day may be measured in the angels' and Spirit's years, increasing its awe and warning.
rows.anchor: burada bu senenin melâike ve Rûh senesi olmak ihtimâliyle günün daha ziyade tehvil ve tahzir ifade etmiş olması da muhtemildir.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some interpret fifty thousand years as a metaphor for the day's severity, without fixing its duration, which could be shorter or longer.
rows.anchor: Bazıları burada elli bin seneden murad tûlün mikdârını beyan değil, o günün şiddetinden kinaye olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Sa‘îd-i Hudrî
rows.claim: A hadith says the day is eased for the believer until it is lighter than a prescribed prayer performed in worldly life.
rows.anchor: Ebu Sa‘îd-i Hudrî’den rivayet olunan bir hadiste إِن َّهُ لَيُخَ َّففُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِ حَت َّى يَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ أَخَ َّف مِنْ صَلاَةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim
rows.claim: He interprets the fifty-thousand-year day as the lifespan of the world, whose elapsed and remaining duration only God knows.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim gibi bazıları bugünü dünyanın ömrü zannetmiş, “ne kadarı geçti, ne kadarı kaldı Allah bilir”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects Abu Muslim's worldly-lifespan reading and considers a day after the world's end more apparent; the majority identify it as the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: doğru değildir. Dünyanın sonuna ait olması daha zâhirdir. Cumhur demişlerdir ki bugünden murad âhiret günü, kıyamet günüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although an eternal afterlife might seem incompatible with a fifty-thousand-year day, the Resurrection includes temporary stages before entry into Paradise or Hell, with different experiences for believers and disbelievers.
rows.anchor: Kıyamet gününün nefhalar beynindeki hengâmları gibi geçici muhtelif devreleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifty-thousand-year period is the standing at judgment, not the whole afterlife; a disbeliever may wait through many such intervals before judgment and entry into Hell.
rows.anchor: mevkıf günüdür. Kâfir hesâbı görülüp cehenneme gönderilinceye kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to wait patiently because the promised punishment has been commanded, or because a valley in Hell will flow like a flood and overtake the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: O hâlde sabret yâ Muhammed! O kâfirlere öyle azab vâki‘olacaktır. Onun emri verilmiştir. Yahut cehennemde bir vâdi sel gibi akmaya başlamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience means fulfilling one's duty with gracious acceptance of God's decree, without letting the disbelievers' disbelief and mockery cause grief.
rows.anchor: bir sabr-ı cemîl güzel bir sabır, kendini elemlendirmeyecek ve Allah’ın takdîrine hüsn-i rızâ ile vazifene bakacak surette bir sabır.
